scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You spend about a third of your life asleep. So what is your brain actually doing all night?

scenes.name: cycles
scenes.text: Sleep comes in cycles of about ninety minutes, moving through light sleep, deep sleep and REM.

scenes.name: deep
scenes.text: In deep sleep, brain waves slow down, and the body focuses on repair and growth.

scenes.name: clean
scenes.text: Research suggests fluid flows through the sleeping brain more, helping wash away waste from the day.

scenes.name: memory
scenes.text: Sleep helps lock in memories, replaying and strengthening what you learned.

scenes.name: rem
scenes.text: In REM sleep, the brain is very active and most vivid dreams happen, while most muscles stay relaxed.

scenes.name: lack
scenes.text: Too little sleep hurts focus, mood and memory. Most adults are advised to get around seven to nine hours.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Repair, clean, save, dream. Sleep is maintenance. Follow for more on how things really work.
